primitives.name: Calcium Dysregulation and Tau Hyperphosphorylation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Excess calcium influx from the extracellular space and increased release from intracellular stores (ER and mitochondria) cause sustained cytosolic calcium elevation. This overload activates kinases (PKC, DYRK1A, CDK5, GSK3β, ERK, CaMKII), proteases (calpains), and co-factors (CaM), while impairing phosphatases (PP2A, CaN), thereby shifting the balance towards phosphorylation.
primitives.assumptions: Calcium influx drives kinase activation and tau phosphorylation via CaM binding.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Neuronal death due to sustained cytosolic calcium elevation.

layer2.mapping: Calcium signaling isomorphically linked to tau aggregation via GSK3β and CaMKII.
layer2.telemetry: Fluorescence imaging of intracellular calcium and tau phosphorylation.

reasoning_traces.think: The mathematical architecture of Alzheimer's Disease (AD) as presented in this chapter window relies fundamentally on a dual-threshold bifurcation model governed by intraneuronal Amyloid Beta (iAβ) concentrations. Initially, iAβ accumulates via standard AβPP proteolysis. This phase is characterized by a slow, linear-to-sublinear growth rate, denoted as the pre-T1 regime. During this period, if the concentration breaches T0, we observe early neuronal damage manifesting as Age-Associated Cognitive Decline (AACD), yet the system retains homeostatic capacity. The critical epistemic leap occurs at threshold T1. Mathematically, T1 acts as a discontinuity point in the derivative of the iAβ concentration function. Crossing T1 triggers the Integrated Stress Response (ISR) via PKR/HRI kinase activation and subsequent eIF2α phosphorylation. This biochemical cascade instantaneously reconfigures the neuronal generative landscape, initiating an AβPP-independent C99 production pathway. Consequently, the system transitions from an externally driven accumulation model to an autonomous, self-sustaining oscillator that aggressively amplifies iAβ levels. This explains the rapid, catastrophic progression of conventional AD once initiated. The proposed therapeutic intervention—ISR suppression—functions as a topological constraint. By pharmacologically inhibiting the ISR, we effectively remove the unstable manifold associated with the AβPP-independent pathway. Even if iAβ crosses T1, the system is mathematically forced to remain on the slow accumulation trajectory, delaying pathology indefinitely.
